questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_L02_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.SYS.3

What is the feasible region of a system?

answer.text: The union of all shaded regions

feedback.text: Union would include points that satisfy only one inequality.
Lines are boundaries, not full feasible regions.
The origin may or may not be feasible.

answer.text: The overlap where all inequalities are true

feedback.text: Correct. Every inequality must be satisfied.

feedback.text: This is not a standard half-plane boundary symbol.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_L02_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.SYS.3

A point in the overlap of two shaded regions means what?

Representation:

RegionMeaning
Shaded by inequality 1Satisfies inequality 1
Shaded by inequality 2Satisfies inequality 2
OverlapSatisfies both inequalities

feedback.text: That would be outside the overlap.
Correct. The overlap is where all constraints are true.

answer.text: It is always on both boundaries

feedback.text: Interior feasible points do not have to lie on boundaries.

answer.text: Solid horizontal boundary and shade below
Dashed horizontal boundary and shade below

feedback.text: Correct. y values less than 5 are below y=5 and equality is excluded.
